###Chapter 1

"You're already married, how can you register again!"

"Don't you know bigamy is a crime?"

…

Evelyn Ross walked out of City Hall in shock.

She held a freshly printed marriage certificate in her hand.

The man who accompanied her looked at her with pity. "Miss Ross, you're already married. Why did you pay me to fake a marriage with you?"

He threw out a final remark before hurrying away. "The deposit is non-refundable."

Evelyn pressed her lips together tightly.

She had never even been in a relationship. How could she possibly be married already?!

She looked down at the printed document.

The girl in the photo had a teardrop mole near the corner of her eye. It was definitely her.

As for the man beside her…

His features were sharp and defined.

He had a tall nose bridge and thin lips that held a faint, almost imperceptible smile.

Even in black and white, his powerful presence was undeniable.

The name field read: Alexander Vance.

She didn't know this man at all!

What was going on?!

Evelyn took a picture of the certificate with her phone.

She opened WhatsApp and sent it to a contact with a black avatar. [Find out who this is for me.]

The reply was instant. [Received.]

Evelyn pushed down her confusion.

She got on her old scooter and drove into an upscale gated community.

Today was her sister Isabella Ashcroft's special day.

Her fiancé was coming to present the dowry.

The Ashcroft house was decorated with lanterns and streamers.

Servants bustled about, busy with preparations.

Evelyn parked her scooter in a corner.

She overheard temporary workers and maids gossiping behind her.

"Who is she? She's so beautiful!"

"Shh, she's the unacknowledged love child."

"Her mother is the mistress. She showed up here pregnant and made a scene, causing the Mrs. to go into early labor. They gave birth on the same day. That old woman has no shame. She clung to the family and refused to leave."

"Miss Ross knows her place, though. She moved out in middle school and hasn't been back for years. I wonder what brings her here today…"

Evelyn pretended not to hear and walked into the living room.

Her mother, Linda Lowell, was waiting by the entrance.

The still attractive woman anxiously pulled her upstairs. "Come with me to see your sister first. Did you get the marriage certificate?"

Evelyn's voice was light. "I got it."

Even though the groom was different, it still counted, right?

"Good. Remember your place. Julian Evans is your sister's fiancé. A top-tier family like that is beyond someone like you. Only your sister is worthy of him!"

A hint of mockery flashed in Evelyn's eyes.

Julian was the eldest grandson of the prestigious Evans family.

He had pursued her for four years in college.

But on graduation day, he proposed to Isabella…

When Linda found out, she demanded Evelyn marry someone immediately.

To sever any possibility with Julian.

It had always been like this…

Whenever her interests conflicted with Isabella's, Linda demanded she yield unconditionally.

Because she was a love child. Her very existence was a sin.

When she was young, she was brainwashed into thinking this was normal.

But she had long since woken up.

Evelyn's expression was serious. "We agreed this is the last time."

Linda was the one who made the mistake.

She was the one who clung to the Ashcroft family to see William every day.

She was the one who wanted to curry favor with Isabella.

Evelyn wouldn't sacrifice her life for Linda's choices.

This was her chance to repay the debt of birth and cut ties.

Linda sounded impatient. "I know."

They arrived at Isabella's room.

The pretty girl sat on a sofa in an elaborate gown, selecting jewelry.

The room was filled with glittering treasures.

Evelyn, in her simple clothes, stood straight-backed.

Isabella noticed her. "Evelyn, what are you doing here?"

Before Evelyn could speak, Linda cut in. "Isabella, Evelyn got married today."

Isabella feigned surprise. "So soon? Who is the man? Is he better than Julian?"

Linda sneered. "Of course not! No one in San Francisco is more prestigious than Mr. Evans! What kind of good family would want her? She married some destitute loser. She didn't even dare bring him here, afraid he'd dirty your eyes!"

Isabella's voice held a hint of jealousy. "How could that be? Evelyn is so beautiful. Otherwise, Julian wouldn't have chased her for four years."

"What use is beauty? Trash belongs with trash. Only lowlifes would marry someone of her status. Mr. Evans just saw her as a toy to play with. Only someone of your status is worthy of him…"

Evelyn frowned.

The man in the photo didn't look or carry himself like a destitute loser.

But she couldn't be bothered to argue.

Isabella finished selecting her jewelry.

She tried to put on her high heels but found her gown too tight to bend over.

Isabella smiled sweetly and looked at Evelyn.

Linda immediately shoved Evelyn. "Useless thing, where are your manners? Your sister can't manage. Help her put her shoes on!"

Evelyn remained silent.

Again.

Did Linda really think she was still that ignorant little girl?

Her gaze was cool. "You can help her yourself."

"Evelyn, what attitude is that? You think you can rebel just because you're married? Your husband is just a freeloader. You'll still need to rely on the Ashcroft family!"

Linda's voice rose. "If you don't get on your sister's good side now, you'll beg for her help someday! The Ashcrofts raised you. You should serve them like a slave!"

A tall figure appeared at the doorway.

It was her father, William Ashcroft.

The man frowned. "An important guest is arriving soon. What is all this noise?"

Isabella stayed silent, playing innocent.

Linda began to cry. "It's this wretched girl. Now that she's married, she looks down on me…"

William turned to Evelyn. "You got married? Why didn't you let the family introduce someone? Where's the marriage certificate? Let me see…"

Faced with her distant father's concern, Evelyn paused, then pulled the printout from her bag.

Linda snatched it away. "Let me see what your useless husband is called!"

Isabella asked curiously, "Dad, who is coming? You seem so nervous."

William thought of that person and felt honored.

He excitedly said a name.

"Alexander Vance."

Evelyn froze completely.

…Who?

###Chapter 2

Isabella looked puzzled. "Who is Alexander Vance? Is he important?"

Evelyn pricked up her ears.

She had been around San Francisco for years, but had never heard that name.

William explained, "He keeps a very low profile. I've never met him myself. He's Julian's uncle. Only twenty-eight, but he's already the true head of the Vance family!"

Linda's eyes lit up. "So he'd be a better match for Isabella than Julian?"

The head of the family was far better than some eldest grandson!

William shot her a warning look. "Don't say such things. Mr. Vance is already married!"

Evelyn narrowed her eyes.

Married...

If he was really the man on the marriage certificate, then he should know the truth.

Linda sighed with regret. "Who is his wife? She must be even luckier than our Isabella."

Evelyn watched William intently.

William shook his head. "No one knows. They say neither of them are social people."

He frowned in thought. "Strange. Why would he suddenly come today..."

The Vances were one of San Francisco's top elite families. Their patriarch held a position of great respect.

The Ashcrofts were only upper-middle class. This marriage was already a step up for them. The patriarch attending the wedding was one thing, but why would he personally come for the dowry discussion?

Linda, however, was smug. "It must be because Isabella is so exceptional! She's caught the attention of the Vance family! Isabella, that necklace isn't grand enough. With elders present today, you need something that shows your status!"

She shoved the printed paper back into Evelyn's hand, eager to pull Isabella away to choose jewelry.

She was more enthusiastic than Sophia, Isabella's own mother.

Evelyn let out a derisive laugh.

"Sir, the Vances have arrived."

The butler reminded William to go downstairs. Passing Evelyn, he said offhandedly, "Since you're here, you might as well stay for a celebratory drink."

Evelyn nodded in agreement.

She was going to stay and meet Alexander Vance!

In the room, Linda helped Isabella put on her jewelry.

Looking at her radiant, beautiful daughter, a flash of triumph shone in her eyes.

Over twenty years ago, if Sophia Ashcroft hadn't interfered, she would have been the one to marry William!

She hated Sophia. She deliberately gave birth on the same day and switched the babies at the hospital.

Now her daughter was marrying into glory, and Sophia had to provide a lavish dowry!

While Evelyn could only marry some lowlife as the illegitimate love child!!

The tables had turned. This was what Sophia owed her!

Downstairs.

Evelyn leaned in the shadows of the staircase, watching the entrance intently.

After some time, Sophia was helped downstairs by a maid. She wore a purple cheongsam, her figure slender, exuding a strong scholarly air.

The maid whispered, "Ma'am, you're not well. You should rest."

Sophia shook her head. "No... It's Isabella's big day... I can't miss it..."

They didn't notice Evelyn and walked towards the entrance.

Evelyn gazed at Sophia's back, her eyes full of affection.

The irony was that Sophia, the one who should hate her, was the only person in the Ashcroft family who had ever shown her warmth.

Linda was never much of a mother. She often forgot to feed her.

As a young child, Evelyn was skin and bones. She learned to scavenge for food from trash cans as soon as she could walk.

Once, Sophia saw her. After that, she started leaving food in the garden every day.

She did this for twelve years.

If not for Sophia, Evelyn would have starved to death.

Hearing Sophia's cough, Evelyn frowned with worry.

Then there was movement at the door. The Vances had arrived!

William and Sophia greeted them at the entrance. After exchanging pleasantries, they stepped aside, and a large group filed in.

Evelyn's eyes immediately found Alexander Vance.

He wore a black custom-tailored suit, walking at the forefront like the center of attention. His face was more defined than in the photo, with sharp contours and a clear jawline.

The man's eyes were deep, his lips thin and cool. Every movement exuded an air of nobility.

Sensing her gaze, the man suddenly looked over.

Their eyes met.

His gaze was sharp, making Evelyn's heart skip a beat. She wanted to study him further, but he had already looked away.

Evelyn was a bit confused.

That reaction... did he know her or not?

William smiled obsequiously. "Mr. Vance, didn't your wife come with you?"

Evelyn felt Alexander's gaze sweep over her again before he replied coolly, "She's unavailable."

They chatted as they moved towards the drawing room.

Julian Evans, who had pursued her for four years, followed behind. The suit made him seem more mature than he was in college. He didn't see Evelyn, distractedly whispering to Isabella.

Everyone crowded around Alexander as he took a seat, discussing the wedding arrangements.

Evelyn stepped out of the shadows.

She stood quietly, observing the lively scene in the drawing room.

Suddenly, her arm was grabbed. Linda hissed in a low voice, "Evelyn, what are you still doing here? Still can't let go of Julian? I'm telling you, he's your sister's fiancé now!"

Evelyn shook off her hand, sneering. "Relax, I have no interest in being a mistress. Mr. Ashcroft asked me to stay for a drink."

Since she was old enough to understand, she had only ever called William "Mr. Ashcroft."

Linda was furious. "That was just politeness! Can't you take a hint? Know your place! Even I can't sit at the table on an occasion like this without embarrassing everyone. How can an illegitimate love child like you? Get out of here now!"

...This was endless!

Evelyn frowned impatiently, about to retort, when she saw Alexander stand up. He gestured to his phone and walked towards the balcony to take a call.

Evelyn's eyes lit up. "Fine, I'm leaving."

After brushing off Linda, she walked out of the drawing room but didn't leave the house. Instead, she turned towards the balcony.

The first-floor balcony connected to a small garden.

Evelyn had just approached when the man on the phone ended his call and his cold, stern gaze swept over her.

Evelyn paused.

Meeting his dangerous eyes, she suddenly curved her lips into a smile and called out carefully, "Husband?"

###Chapter 3

A glass door muffled the lively chatter from the drawing room.

Evelyn Ross stared directly at Alexander Vance.

Hearing that form of address, the man’s entire demeanor turned icy.
His eyes darkened, radiating a chilling coldness.
His expression remained blank as he turned to leave.

Evelyn quickly stepped in front of him, blocking his path.

Alexander frowned.
"Move aside."

His voice was deep, each word laced with an aristocratic chill.
It made her heart itch strangely.

Evelyn sensed something was off.
"You don't know me?"

Alexander looked down at her.
"Should I know you?"

He had felt a pair of eyes on him since entering the Ashcroft residence.
The gaze was bold, unlike the fawning looks from others.
He had glanced over a couple of times.
The girl was beautiful, with fair skin and bright eyes.
A teardrop mole near her eye added a touch of allure.
She seemed docile on the surface, but an untamed spirit lurked beneath.
Even after he noticed her staring, she didn't look away.
She met his gaze directly.
He had thought she was different.
But she was even bolder, addressing him as 'husband' right away...

Impatience flashed in Alexander's eyes.
"Miss, I am a married man. Please show some respect."

Evelyn was stunned.

He didn't know her, yet claimed to be married?
Did City Hall make a mistake?

She asked, "Who is your wife?"

"That is none of your concern."

The four words were frigid.

Evelyn pulled out a copy of her marriage certificate.
"Mr. Vance, is this you?"

Alexander looked at the document.
His eyes fell on the woman's name: Evelyn Ross.
He glanced up, his expression mocking.
"Miss Ashcroft, if you're going to forge a document, at least do it professionally."

He stepped around her and walked straight toward the parking lot.

Evelyn tried to follow, but two bodyguards in black suits stopped her.
She called after his retreating back, "The certificate is real! You can check at City Hall..."

Alexander didn't look back.
He got into his car and drove away.

His private assistant returned to the drawing room and encountered Isabella Ashcroft.

Isabella had just witnessed Evelyn pestering Alexander, but hadn't heard their conversation.
Seeing Alexander leave and Evelyn chase after him on her scooter, she immediately asked, "Why did Mr. Vance leave? Did someone offend him?"

The assistant smiled politely.
"Mr. Vance had urgent business to attend to. Please convey his apologies to the elders."

Since his boss hadn't ordered the girl to be taught a lesson, he was letting it slide.

Isabella nodded and politely saw the assistant out.

The wedding date was settled.
The Vance family left after lunch.

Once the guests were gone, William Ashcroft expressed concern.
"Why did Mr. Vance leave early? Was our hospitality lacking?"

Isabella thought of Julian Evans's distracted behavior all day, his eyes constantly searching the room.
She also recalled Evelyn's face.
Her fists clenched.
Her eyes shifted nervously.
"Father, I saw Evelyn harassing Mr. Vance. She angered him so much he left. Mr. Vance even left a message..."

"What message?"

"He said you should discipline your daughter properly." Isabella bit her lip.
"With Evelyn acting like this, the Vances will think we have poor family morals."

William's face darkened with anger.

Evelyn rode her electric scooter out of the villa district, but had already lost sight of him.

She was feeling frustrated when her phone rang.

It was James Klein, her subordinate.
"Boss, a lot of people are investigating Dr. Nan."

Evelyn raised an eyebrow.
"Did we get exposed?"

"Of course not! Who would guess the brilliant mind who cracked hydrogen fuel is a freshly graduated young woman..."

"Get to the point," Evelyn interrupted him.

"Right, right. We found information on Alexander Vance! Second son of the Vance family. Rumored to have a violent temper. Sent abroad as a child. Everyone thought the family business would go to his older brother. But he returned last week unexpectedly. Used ruthless methods to force the old man to step down. Now he controls the Vance Group."

James was curious.
"I thought you found someone easy to control for a marriage of convenience? How did the groom turn into this cold-faced king of hell? Boss, an unstable marital status could affect the company's IPO..."

Evelyn frowned.
"Find his contact information and schedule. I need to speak with him again."

She had agreed to Linda Lowell's demand for an immediate marriage only because having a married status as the company's legal representative was beneficial for the IPO.
Now she was inexplicably married, entangled in some unknown scheme.
Alexander's identity was complicated.
It was best to get a divorce quickly to avoid further trouble.

She ended the call and rubbed her temples.

This was troublesome.
Alexander traveled with bodyguards.
Getting close to him wouldn't be easy.
She shouldn't have called him 'husband' today and angered him...

She sighed, started her beat-up scooter, and slowly headed home.

Leaving the city center, she returned to the old urban village in the suburbs.
She had rented this old place when she moved out of the Ashcroft home in middle school, back when she had no money.
She had grown accustomed to it and never moved.

As she turned the corner toward home, an elderly woman suddenly darted into the road!

Evelyn slammed on the brakes, nearly hitting her.

The old woman didn't seem like a scam artist.
She was dressed well, unlike an ordinary person.
A placard hung around her neck with a contact number and the words: Reward if found.

...Alzheimer's.
Someone's grandmother was lost.

Evelyn took out her phone and entered the number.

The dazed old woman suddenly grabbed her wrist.
Her cloudy eyes lit up.
"Granddaughter-in-law! You are my granddaughter-in-law!"

Evelyn gave a wry smile.

Single for 22 years, and now she had another husband?
Was City Hall handing them out wholesale today?

She found it amusing and asked casually, "Grandmother, who is your grandson?"

The old woman frowned in thought.
What was her grandson's name...?
Oh, Alexander Vance!!
###Chapter 4

Granddaughter-in-law!

The old lady strained to remember.
"He's called... Vance... Vance something..."
The name was on the tip of her tongue, but she just couldn't get it out.
The elderly woman grew frustrated, slapping her thigh in agitation.

Evelyn Ross spoke softly to soothe her.
"Don't rush. Take your time."
She took out her phone and dialed a number.

At that exact moment, on a nearby street.
The atmosphere inside the Bentley was oppressive.
Alexander Vance's face was like dark water.
Thomas Watson reported nervously, "Mrs. Vance gave the bodyguards the slip and ran off by herself..."
A chill emanated from the man.
Surveillance showed the elderly woman had taken a bus to the suburbs.
This area had sparse camera coverage, making the search difficult.

The abrupt ring of a phone broke the silence.
Alexander pressed the answer button.
A lazy female voice came through the receiver. "Hello. Your elderly relative is with me."
The temperature in the car seemed to drop instantly.
Thomas immediately began tracing the signal source.
Alexander's voice was icy. "Name your price."
"...Just kidding," the girl said cheerfully. "Remember to keep a better eye on her."
She gave an address and hung up.

Thomas let out a long sigh of relief.
That good Samaritan really knew how to joke!
A flicker of recognition passed through Alexander's eyes.
That voice... where had he heard it before?

Five minutes later, they arrived at the location.
They found the old lady waiting with a police officer.
Alexander stepped forward. "Grandmother, what are you doing all the way out here?"
The old woman whispered mysteriously, "Looking for my granddaughter-in-law! She lives around here!"
Alexander sighed helplessly. "You're confused again..."
"I really saw her!" the old lady complained. "That girl handed me over to the police and slipped away... Let me borrow your phone."
She took the phone and carefully noted down the number that had just called.
Her little notebook finally had the granddaughter-in-law's contact information!

Evelyn hated dealing with grateful scenes.
Seeing a patrol officer, she promptly handed over the elderly woman and left.
Early the next morning, her advisor called, urging her to come in.
Evelyn rode her scooter to the university.

Inside Professor Lowell's office, Isabella Ashcroft and Linda Lowell were already waiting.
Evelyn narrowed her peach-blossom eyes.
She and Isabella attended the same university but had vastly different experiences.
Isabella had gloriously tested into San Francisco University.
Evelyn had deliberately scored low to enter the obscure Energy and Power Engineering major, aiming to manage her company.
Then, new energy suddenly became a hot field.
Isabella immediately transferred departments, becoming her classmate once again.
Linda's presence was a surprise.

Professor Lowell looked grave. "Evelyn, your guaranteed graduate admission has been revoked."
Evelyn raised an eyebrow. "On what grounds?"
"Your mother reported you for misconduct," Professor Lowell said, frowning. "Quickly apologize to your mother. Don't ruin your future!"
Isabella spoke up gently. "Professor Lowell, Mom only wants what's best for Evelyn."
She turned to Evelyn. "You offended Mr. Vance. He said he wants you to disappear from San Francisco."
Evelyn was taken aback.
Alexander didn't seem the petty type.
Isabella, however... was an expert at spinning tales.

Isabella held out a plane ticket. "Dad wants you to lay low in Argentina."
Evelyn glanced at the destination.
The other side of the planet.
The Ashcrofts were clearly afraid she might return.
She pushed the ticket away. "Not necessary."
Isabella then produced a bank card. "This fifty thousand is what I've saved. You can use it for now..."
Linda snatched the card back. "Isabella, are you stupid? The Ashcrofts paying for the ticket is already more than enough!"
She commanded Evelyn, "Withdraw from school and go abroad immediately!"
Evelyn met her gaze coldly. "What gives you the right to decide for me?"
"The fact that I'm your mother! Do you think you can even graduate? Getting a job and earning money is what you should be doing!"
Professor Lowell quickly interjected, "Mrs. Lowell, you're mistaken! Evelyn's performance in her major is exceptional..."
Linda cut him off directly. "Professor, don't cover for her! The only reason she wants a graduate degree is to compete with Isabella! She should look in the mirror and see if she's even worthy!"
The crude language left the professor speechless.

Isabella smiled, smoothing things over. "I was admitted through a special recruitment channel."
Professor Lowell was curious. "Which professor recruited you specially?"
Isabella pretended to be modest. "It was Dr. Nan. He just patented a new hydrogen fuel."
Evelyn's head snapped up. "You said who?"
###Chapter 5

Dr. Nan?

When had she ever said she would specially recruit Isabella?

Professor Lowell said in surprise, "You know Dr. Nan?"

Isabella smiled gracefully. "It's quite a coincidence, actually. My mother sponsored Dr. Nan's education years ago. After he achieved success, he sought out our family to repay the kindness. He's provided technical support for our family company all these years. He's always been very accommodating to my requests."

Evelyn raised an eyebrow.

She had contacted Sophia Ashcroft using the "Dr. Nan" identity to repay her for raising her.

When had she ever been accommodating to Isabella's requests?

She was really good at taking credit.

Professor Lowell, however, believed her. "Which university does Dr. Nan work for now?"

Isabella replied, "I've promised the Dean I would invite Dr. Nan to teach here."

"Excellent!" Professor Lowell beamed. He looked at Evelyn. "Evelyn, your research aligns perfectly with Dr. Nan's. I'll introduce you when he arrives. If Dr. Nan speaks for you, there might still be a chance to salvage your graduate position!"

Isabella feigned concern. "Professor, is that feasible? The Vance family is, after all, the wealthiest in San Francisco. They provide substantial research funding to the university every year..."

Professor Lowell waved it off. "Dr. Nan is highly sought after now. I heard Cambridge and Oxford have both extended invitations. Numerous companies are competing to invest in his work. If he intervenes, the university will undoubtedly choose him!"

Isabella sighed. "But Dr. Nan is only helping out of respect for my mother. Evelyn is my father's... love child. Her position is opposed to my mother's... Evelyn, perhaps I could ask Dr. Nan for you?"

Evelyn declined. "That won't be necessary."

Isabella's performance was utterly ridiculous.

A faint smile touched Evelyn's lips as she addressed Professor Lowell. "Professor, it's really not worth the trouble. You know I never planned on graduate school anyway."

Professor Lowell's expression was full of regret.

He was the one who had discovered Evelyn's talent and insisted she pursue the graduate position.

He never expected things to turn out this way.

His eyes reddened slightly. "Then let me write you a letter of recommendation for a job."

Linda scoffed. "Don't waste your effort! After offending Mr. Vance, she thinks she can find a job in San Francisco? She's delusional!"

Professor Lowell retorted angrily, "I refuse to believe anyone holds absolute power in this city! If she can't find a job, she can be my teaching assistant! I insist on having her!"

Warmth spread through Evelyn's heart. "Professor, it's just a misunderstanding between Mr. Vance and me. Once it's cleared up, everything will be fine. Please don't worry."

Professor Lowell sighed. "If it gets resolved, come back. You'll still be my student."

Evelyn's voice softened. "Alright. I'll definitely come back."

Teaching at San Francisco University wouldn't be a bad option.

Isabella clenched her fingers.

She didn't understand. She was the top student. Why did Professor Lowell favor the utterly ordinary Evelyn?

Was the old fool also bewitched by her face?

Furious, Isabella glanced at Linda. "Evelyn, are you still planning to pester Mr. Vance? He's married. Your behavior is truly inappropriate..."

Linda predictably exploded in rage.

Slap!

The sound of the slap echoed through the office.

Evelyn's cheek burned with a sharp, stinging pain.

She hadn't expected Linda to hit her right in front of Professor Lowell!

Linda showed no remorse. She pointed a finger and yelled, "You shameless brat! Has a few years away made you forget the rules at home? Apologize to your sister this instant! Promise you will never see the Vances again!"

Evelyn's eyes turned completely cold.

It seemed her words about it being "the last time" the other day had made no impression.

Linda still saw her as that meek, pathetic pushover.

Since reason didn't work, she couldn't blame her for not holding back...

Isabella secretly gloated.

When they were young, Evelyn was subservient to her, never fighting back.

After they reunited in university, Evelyn actually dared to stand tall.

A few years without discipline, and she forgot her place!

Today, Linda would teach her a lesson.

Isabella was still thinking this when she saw Evelyn walk over. She assumed she was coming to apologize.

Isabella's lips had just begun to curve into a smile—

Evelyn suddenly raised her hand and slapped Isabella hard across the face, twice!

Slap! Slap!

Isabella was stunned by the blows.

Linda roared and charged forward. "Evelyn, have you lost your mind!"

Evelyn whirled around!

Her gaze was sinister, like a vengeful spirit. A chilling aura of menace radiated from her.

Linda was frightened into stillness. "You... what do you think you're doing? I'm your mother! How dare you raise your hand against me? You unfilial beast!"

"You failed as a mother. Don't blame me for failing as a daughter!"

Evelyn's voice was icy. "Stay out of my life. Whatever you do to me, I will return it to Isabella twofold!"

She turned and bowed deeply to Professor Lowell. "Thank you for your guidance these past four years. I will be back."

With that, she turned and left.

It wasn't until her figure disappeared that Linda snapped out of it. She rushed to Isabella. "Isabella, are you alright? That wretch actually dared to hit you! The world is upside down!"

Isabella touched her swollen cheek, trembling with rage. "Where does she get the nerve?"

Linda was stunned. "Could Mr. Vance actually be interested in her? Impossible. She's married. Why would Mr. Vance want used goods..."

Isabella had the same thought.

But thinking of Evelyn's face, she felt a flicker of doubt...

Professor Lowell was shocked by the spectacle.

He looked at Linda in disbelief, listening to the vile language. He couldn't help but wonder:

Was this really Evelyn's mother? Not Isabella's?

Perhaps it was his imagination, but Professor Lowell suddenly thought the two looked somewhat alike...

Evelyn had just left the campus when James called.

"Boss, it's all clear now! I know why Alexander Vance claims to be married but doesn't recognize you!"
###Chapter 6

The school gate was bustling with activity.

Groups of energetic students walked by in twos and threes.

Evelyn Ross stood by the roadside, pushing her scooter.

She pressed her tongue against her swollen lip, her voice slightly hoarse. "Go on."

"The Vance Group appears prosperous, but the internal power struggles are vicious. The old patriarch favors the eldest son and is determined to pass the family business to him. Alexander Vance, as the youngest son, has faced significant suppression over the years."

"A few years back, the patriarch forced several arranged marriage candidates on Alexander. It was quite the scandal. Eventually, Alexander publicly declared he had already married a girl from an ordinary family, which finally quieted the rumors."

"The interesting part is, this so-called wife has never made a public appearance. She never attends any Vance family gatherings."

"So the truth is…"

James Klein deliberately dragged out his words, trying to build suspense.

Evelyn cut him off directly. "Understood. His schedule and contact info?"

James was left speechless, replying sullenly, "Schedule's in your email. Can't get his private number. Someone at his level has extremely tight security."

Evelyn remained calm. "Doesn't matter. I'll intercept him."

James immediately perked up. "He has plenty of bodyguards. Planning a direct approach or something more subtle?"

"Need to keep a low profile recently." Evelyn gave a lazy, roguish smile. "Besides, I'm a woman. A direct confrontation isn't suitable."

James was left utterly speechless.

The Vance Group tower soared into the clouds, dominating the most prosperous area of downtown.

Evelyn changed into a delivery uniform and entered the lobby carrying a cardboard box.

She showed her work ID to the receptionist. "A package for Mr. Vance. Requires his personal signature."

After the receptionist confirmed with the secretary's office, she was allowed upstairs.

The elevator went straight to the eighty-eighth floor.

As the doors opened, the view expanded dramatically.

The entire floor was the secretarial workspace, with over a hundred elite employees serving Alexander Vance exclusively.

Evelyn followed the guiding secretary towards the CEO's office.

After knocking, a deep male voice came from inside. "Enter."

Just as Evelyn was about to relax, a tall, lean figure stopped her.

Thomas Watson, the special assistant, scrutinized her with a furrowed brow. "Miss Ross? Why is it you?"

Yesterday she was pestering the boss at the Ashcroft residence, and today she dares to impersonate a delivery person to get up here?

Thomas looked displeased, signaling for security. "How did they let just anyone in? Escort her out immediately!"

"I will never forgive the person who killed my child."

"Let's get a divorce."

She leaned on Evelyn's shoulder.

"Evelyn, take me away from here."

"Okay."

Evelyn supported her as they walked step by step out the main door.

Once in the car, Mina finally broke down crying.

"My baby..."

Evelyn comforted her softly. "Don't cry. Actually..."
###Chapter 447

Mina Sherwood's heart felt as if it were being shredded.

The months of her pregnancy had been pure torment.

No one believed her.

She had endured until the third month, when she could finally undergo an amniocentesis with Marcus Valentine.

The reporters had ruined everything.

She knew Marcus had been provoked.

She could understand his actions.

But she could not forgive the pain he caused.

Mina smiled bitterly.

A heavy, dragging sensation settled in her lower abdomen.

It had been two hours since she took the pill.

Was the baby leaving her now?

Evelyn Ross spoke suddenly. "The baby is actually fine."

Mina was stunned. "What?"

She smiled mockingly. "Grace, you don't need to comfort me. After taking an abortion pill, even if it doesn't work, the baby won't be healthy."

Evelyn cleared her throat softly. "I switched the abortion pill for a vitamin."

Mina froze.

Alexander Vance strode over. "I discovered Marcus had bought the abortion pill and told Evelyn. She found an opportunity to go home and switch them."

Mina was bewildered. "How did you discover he bought the pill?"

Alexander paused.

It was when Evelyn had forced him to go get Marcus to sign the divorce agreement.

He hadn't wanted to interfere in a couple's affairs.

But Evelyn had been insistent.

He had people track Marcus's movements and accidentally discovered the purchase.

Alexander gave a light cough. "I happened to see it."

Mina frowned. "But my stomach hurts."

"Psychosomatic."

Evelyn's words were direct and precise.

Mina was silent for a moment.

She focused on the sensation. "It... really doesn't seem to hurt anymore."

Evelyn supported her arm. "The choice is yours now. Tell Marcus, or don't tell him?"

Mina looked down.

If she told him, he definitely wouldn't want the divorce.

Better not to say anything.

She didn't want to use Marcus.

Her husband's lack of trust had exhausted her.

She truly wanted a divorce.

If not for Evelyn, he would have killed their child.

She wasn't a saint.

The baby being okay didn't absolve his despicable behavior.

Mina made her decision. "I want to go somewhere no one knows me. Raise the baby in peace. Live my life."

"Stay at the Nan family home," Evelyn said directly. "I'd worry about you alone in a strange place."

Marcus's oligospermia still needed to be investigated.

If someone was targeting Marcus, would they harm Mina if they knew her baby wasn't terminated?

Evelyn felt the situation was becoming complex.

She helped Mina into the car, and Alexander joined them.

Alexander took the driver's seat.

Evelyn and Mina sat in the back.

During the drive, Mina bowed her head, tears falling.

Evelyn didn't know how to comfort her, just gently patted her hand.

Mina wiped her tears. "Grace, I'm okay."

She looked at Alexander in the driver's seat. "Boy Toy, thank you this time."

Alexander was about to offer a polite response.

Mina continued. "Evelyn, I think you should just be with this Boy Toy. That Alexander Vance isn't right for you... His wife just died, and he went to the Ashcroft family reunion gala with a dowry. He's clearly not a good man."

Alexander: "..."

He suddenly felt a twinge of regret for helping her.

...

At the Evans residence.

Justin Evans stormed into the house and found Mrs. Evans.

"Mom, I was played!"

Mrs. Evans looked at him coldly. "You're a fool. Who else is to blame?"

Justin threw his phone in front of her. "Look! They set me up! They talked about oligospermia, so I believed it! Now look!"

He pointed angrily at the news on the TV. "The child is his! It was all a farce! He used the chance to promote a new product, staged that scene in the car refusing to get out, let people try to smash it without success. Acted like it was real! The stock price shot up instantly!"

Mrs. Evans's face was dark.

She looked at Justin. "I heard Evelyn Ross wanted to cooperate with our family, made inquiries before. Whatever her goal was, cooperation is out of the question now!"

She picked up Justin's phone. "This report, didn't you verify it before sending it?"

Justin was even more aggrieved. "I did verify it! He went for the check-up, and it just happened to be at our family's hospital! Would our own doctor lie to me? Who knew there'd be this kind of twist!"

Mrs. Evans gave the butler a look.

The butler immediately went to investigate.

He returned five minutes later. "The doctor is indeed ours. No issues."

Justin was puzzled. "Then what happened?"

Mrs. Evans was exasperated. "He has his own hospital. Why go to ours? He must have switched the samples! He was setting this up a month ago! Devious!"

Justin fumed. "The Valentines are too cunning! They seem honest, but they're like this!"

Mrs. Evans sighed.

She exited Justin's text messages, about to return the phone, when her eyes caught an unread message.

Unknown Sender: [Hello, I am the owner of that jade piece. May I ask who you are?]

Mrs. Evans froze.

She sharply turned to Justin. "This message, why haven't you read it?!"

Justin cared most about his sister's situation.

When placing the external advertisement, they had used his number.

Justin was also stunned. "I've been busy with the Valentine matter recently, missed a lot of messages. Could this be... sister?"

Mrs. Evans urged. "Go contact them immediately!"

Justin quickly nodded. "Right, it must be sister! Technology is advanced now, no one would falsely claim this!"
###Chapter 448

The Evans family set up a DNA verification requirement after posting the missing person ad.

This prevented any imposters from coming forward.

Occasionally, someone would provide a vague lead, claiming to have seen the jade pendant.

The Evans family would purchase all such information and verify each one meticulously.

Finding their lost daughter became the family's top priority.

Even the business war with the Ashcrofts was left for Justin Evans to handle alone.

This led to frequent oversights and mistakes.

The eldest and second Evans brothers had no time to spare for other matters.

Justin Evans made a phone call.

The call was disconnected.

He stared blankly at his mother.

As he was about to redial, a message arrived: [Can I help you?]

Justin called again.

It was disconnected once more.

Another message popped up: [I can't talk right now. Who is this?]

Justin stamped his foot in frustration. "Why won't our sister answer the call?"

Mrs. Evans tapped his head. "Your sister should be in college now. She might be in class. Send a text."

Justin immediately replied: [Sister, it's your brother!]

...

Hospital corridor.

Jane Evans and her classmates listened to their supervisor's instructions.

She was a medical student in her final year of internship.

Outstanding performance could secure her a permanent position at the hospital.

Her phone vibrated.

Seeing the message, her fingers trembled slightly.

The other party's high-profile search suggested immense wealth and influence.

Why would such a family lose a daughter?

Whether she was abandoned or not, she needed answers.

Jane lowered her head to type a reply.

The supervisor suddenly called out. "Jane Evans, Peng Hui. You'll take the third-floor VIP suites. Mind your manners."

Jane nodded.

Peng Hui acknowledged.

They headed toward the elevator.

Someone muttered under their breath. "Why assign a mute to the VIP floor?"

The supervisor frowned. "No questions."

He watched Jane's retreating figure with a complex expression.

Though mute, Jane was brilliant. She should have focused on research.

Unfortunately, she had offended the second branch of the Evans family.

Young Master Jason Evans had specifically requested she be "taken care of."

The hospital was Evans property. The supervisor was powerless to intervene.

He could only sigh inwardly at Jane's misfortune.

...

Jane was filled with hope.

Peng Hui encouraged her. "You're top of your class. You'll definitely get to stay."

Jane nodded emphatically.

After graduation, she could earn money to support her brother.

Her brother had endured countless hardships for her education.

She was determined to succeed.

They made their rounds through the VIP suites.

Peng Hui whispered a reminder. "These clients are wealthy and powerful. Impress them, and you'll secure your spot."

Jane nodded again.

They pushed open the door to room 306.

Jane met Jason Evans's cold gaze.

She turned to flee.

"Stop!"

Jason barked.

Peng Hui offered an apologetic smile. "Is something wrong, sir?"

Jason pointed to his abdomen. "My wound might have reopened. Check it for me."

Peng Hui stepped forward to lift the covers.

Jason pointed at Jane. "I want her to do it."

Peng Hui froze.

Jason sneered. "Do doctors have genders? Can't handle it? Then get out!"

Jane clenched her fists.

Jason roared. "Get over here!"

Jane approached with trembling steps.

She uncovered the bandage.

The wound was perfectly intact.

Jason suddenly kicked her hard in the chest. "You bitch! Trying to kill me with pain?"

Jane staggered backward.

She hurriedly pulled out paper and pen. [I didn't touch you!]

Jason laughed scornfully. "A mute doctor? Diagnosing with gestures? If you don't satisfy me today, I'll make sure you never practice medicine again!"
###Chapter 449

Jane Evans' pupils constricted sharply.
She stared fixedly at Jason Evans.

Her eyes reddened.
Her nails dug into her palms.

After a long moment, she took a deep breath.
She crossed out the words she had just written and started again.
[How may I assist you?]

Jason Evans let out a derisive laugh when he saw the line.
"You know what's good for you. You understand that pleasing me is your only way out!"

He pointed to the fruit platter.
"Go wash the fruit and cut it into small pieces. Remove every single strand of pith from the oranges. I hate that stuff."

Peng Hui couldn't help speaking up.
"That's not an intern's job…"

Jason sneered.
"You know it's an internship? Do you want to get hired full-time or not?"

A bodyguard barked sharply.
"Open your damn eyes! This is the Evans family young master! The entire hospital belongs to the Evans family! The young master can make you disappear with one word! Shut your mouth!"

Peng Hui was frightened into silence.

Jason stared at Jane.
"Are you going or not?"

Jane bit her lip and nodded.
She picked up the fruit platter and walked out of the room.

She wiped her tears at the corridor corner.
She turned on the faucet and began washing the fruit.

A familiar voice suddenly came from behind her.
"Jane Evans?"

Jane turned around and saw Evelyn Ross standing not far away.
Her eyes instantly lit up.
She hurriedly pulled out her pen and paper, but before she could write anything, Evelyn spoke.
"I'm here to take care of something. What are you doing here?"

Evelyn had come for Marcus Valentine's azoospermia report.

Marcus clearly had normal fertility with high sperm motility.
Why did three hospitals all issue azoospermia diagnoses?

She had come today to confront the attending physician.
But she was told he had suddenly gone abroad for an exchange program last night.
It was a wasted trip.

Just as she was feeling disappointed, she bumped into a familiar figure.

Jane wrote on the paper: I am interning here.

Evelyn raised an eyebrow.
"Medical major?"

Jane nodded.

Evelyn was about to speak when she suddenly remembered Jason was on this floor.
Her brow furrowed tightly.
"Jason hasn't given you trouble? Do you need me to help you transfer departments?"

Jane quickly waved her hands.

She didn't want to trouble Miss Evelyn again.
Getting the heirloom back last time was already an enormous favor.

Thanks to that pendant, she could return to the Evans family…

She unconsciously touched the pendant at her neck.
She felt its outline through the fabric of her clothes.

Evelyn wanted to say something more, but footsteps suddenly sounded from the end of the corridor.

Justin Evans and Mrs. Evans walked side by side.

Justin swiped his phone irritably.
"Mom, my sister still isn't replying to messages. Her phone's GPS is on this floor. Which one is her?"

He looked up and saw Evelyn and Jane.
His face instantly darkened.
"What are you doing here?"

Evelyn pulled Jane behind her.
"Did your family open this hospital? Can I not come?"

Justin sneered.
"I'll hang a sign right now: The Ashcrofts and dogs are not allowed!"

Evelyn raised an eyebrow.
"Does the hospital pick its patients?"

"So what if it does? The Evans family's hospital. I call the shots!"

Evelyn scoffed.
"Dare to say that publicly?"

Justin choked.
"You…!"

Mrs. Evans pulled her son back.
She gave Evelyn a cold look.
"Miss Evelyn, you're carrying a voice recorder, aren't you? Deliberately provoking my son to get material to use against the Evans family?"

Evelyn rolled her eyes.
"I'm not that bored. I'm here to check my brother's azoospermia report."

Justin flew into a rage.
"Stop pretending! Wasn't it your brother who switched the samples? Used azoospermic semen for the test and then framed us? How could the Evans family hospital's report be fake!"

Evelyn narrowed her eyes.
"Are you sure the report is real?"

"Of course! This is a hospital, not a joke!"

Justin glared at her.
"Trying to bring down the Evans family this way? Dream on!"

Evelyn retorted coldly.
"Then why did the attending physician suddenly go abroad last night? His phone is unreachable."

Justin was stunned.
"What?"

"The doctor who examined Marcus Valentine flew abroad last night. Completely lost contact."

Justin frowned.
"More of your tricks? Bribed the doctor, then shifted the blame to the Evans family? The Ashcrofts are truly vicious!"

Evelyn: "…"

She curled her lip.
"Paranoia is an illness. You should get it treated."

Justin: ?

Evelyn couldn't be bothered to argue.
She pulled Jane forward.
"Don't act so high and mighty. Arranging her internship on the third floor—isn't it just to make it convenient for Jason to get revenge?"

Justin smirked.
"I don't have time to manage such a minor character. Just some stray girl. You crippled Jason for her. What's wrong with the Evans family venting some anger?"

Evelyn was about to retort when Mrs. Evans cut her son off.
"Don't waste time on trivial matters."

Justin suddenly remembered.

He was here to find his sister!

Why was he wasting words with Evelyn!

He shot Evelyn a fierce glare.

###Chapter 450

The call was disconnected after just one ring.

A cold, automated voice sounded from the receiver.
"Hello, the number you have dialed is unavailable."

Justin Evans frowned deeply.

Where was his sister?

He sent another message.
[Sis, Mom and I are here. Which floor are you on? We'll come find you!]

The message went unanswered.

Justin grew increasingly anxious.

Mrs. Evans frowned.
"What's wrong?"

Justin sighed.
"No reply. She's not answering her calls."

Mrs. Evans took a deep breath.
"Secure the entire building immediately. Screen everyone who appears to be around her age."

Justin nodded.
"Alright."

He immediately instructed his subordinates to act.

While waiting for the bodyguards to arrive, Mrs. Evans spoke.
"I'll guard the entrance. Since you're here, go check on Jason."

Justin agreed.

Mrs. Evans turned and headed downstairs.

Justin walked toward Jason's room.
He suddenly turned back to look at Jane, his expression dark.
"It just occurred to me that Jason arranged for you to be a medical intern on this floor, correct?"
"Since that's the case, come here immediately and attend to Jason properly!"
"Otherwise…"

Jane clenched her fists, her eyes reddening.

Evelyn Ross stopped her.
"Jane, you don't have to subject yourself to this."

Jane shook her head.

She had to become a doctor.

She had studied medicine for so many years precisely for this goal.

Both her brother and she had been accepted into university back then.
Their family was too poor.
Her brother had given his spot to her.

Her brother had said that even though she couldn't speak, she could definitely become a great doctor.
Perhaps even develop a medicine to treat her vocal cords, allowing her to call him "brother" just once…

Low-key. Mysterious.

###Chapter 610

She laughed arrogantly, her eyes triumphant.

Evelyn watched her quietly, then suddenly curved her lips. "You're not leaving yet."

Nicole Sterling froze. "Why? Is your Special Operations Division going back on its word? Not admitting defeat after losing the match?"

The curve of Evelyn's lips deepened. "Because I won."

Those words made Nicole Sterling completely stiffen.

She stared in disbelief, her eyes wide. "What did you say?"

"I said, I won." Evelyn enunciated each word clearly. "Now, it's time for you to fulfill the bet. Tell me, where exactly is the Sterling Family?"
###Chapter 633

Evelyn Ross sat across from Nicole Sterling.

Her posture was composed.

Four and a half months ago...

That was exactly when she and her sister were attacked in San Francisco, and their mother was taken.

It matched.

The Sterling Family was indeed cautious.

They even guarded against their own people.

Evelyn didn't know.

Had her sister, Grace Sterling, been summoned and refused? Or had she never been summoned at all?

He began slowly. "Your sister... when she was in the Sterling Family, she was actually quite special."
###Chapter 634

Isabella had never experienced any external interference.

Her sister's adoptive parents might have come about this way.

Chloe.

Because the Sterling Family was struggling to have descendants?

The Fox.

###Chapter 671

She was truly alive.

As long as she could be happy, that was enough.

This wasn't a dream.

Not a dream.

As soon as the words left his mouth.

"She's right."

The Evelyn he wanted was forever out of his reach.

Besides her, what else did he want?

He wanted his father to stay home.

He wanted his parents to get along.

He wanted a complete family.

He wanted his father to have no mistress, no illegitimate daughter…

He would never get them.

So now, what did he actually want?

At her age, Eleanor often suffered from internal heat and a burning stomach. Cool, crisp apples were something she usually enjoyed.

When Cecilia said, "It's all because Uncle Alexander monopolized you, that's why we couldn't come see you," did a part of Eleanor believe it?

###Chapter 706

Alexander Vance's brow furrowed.

###Chapter 707

An address.

Robert Vance was diagnosed with Alzheimer's.

Home.

So guilty.

On one side were vitamins. On the other was the special medication.

A ten percent discount meant nine hundred thousand.

Aaron wouldn't live more than two weeks?

Next time she bought the medication, she'd take the four million and go abroad.

It seemed like anemia.

Evelyn Ross woke up in the morning and immediately prepared to go to the Truman family home.

Aaron's eyes reddened, and he hugged her tightly. "How could you be so foolish! If you're gone, what use is money to me?"

Cecilia burst into loud sobs.

Aaron's eyes also welled up.

But at that moment, Sebastian Truman and Mia Truman exchanged a glance and slowly stood up.

Evelyn Ross also raised an eyebrow.

If she heard correctly...

Cecilia's sobs cut off abruptly.

Aaron froze, looking blankly at Sebastian.

Sebastian's tone remained even. "Just now, she kept saying you had colon cancer. Who was the special medicine prescribed for? Have you forgotten?"

Aaron shuddered.

He slowly turned his head, looking at Cecilia in his arms with disbelief.

Cecilia's face instantly turned as pale as a sheet.
###Chapter 783

Cecilia Evans froze.

She immediately explained, "Aaron, don't believe him! I had no idea you were sick. I just thought taking too much medicine was bad, so I switched them for vitamins! I really didn't know!"

Sebastian looked at his younger brother.

Usually quite smart, good at studies, sharp in company matters.

How did his brain just stop working the moment Cecilia was involved?

To cut her own life short?

It was to show the Truman family wouldn't go easy.

Because Cecilia didn't have long to live, the Trumans had to prioritize her.

With colon cancer, about to die...

She had looked it up. People didn't live long with this disease.

And on top of that, she had taken the medicine she herself had put in...

She didn't want to die.

Even if she had to die, she wouldn't let those left behind live in peace!

She understood perfectly how to provoke Aaron.

An enemy they couldn't easily get rid of.

Because he was a Truman.

###Chapter 784

The surveillance footage clearly showed her, taking advantage of a moment when no one was looking, pouring a packet of powder into her own water glass.

She had miscalculated.

###Chapter 785

Aaron Truman was in a state of utter shock.

Cecilia, you really haven't changed at all.

This time, I won't let you get away.
###Chapter 786

This man.

Not father and daughter.

Did Zack know?

"We must get to the bottom of this."
###Chapter 794

The peaceful life she and her mother had in San Francisco... was actually under Elara's protection?

"You've finally come back. Spend more time with her. All these years you haven't been home, but she's always kept an eye on you. The account password was the key credential for claiming inheritance rights. Without it, she wouldn't even qualify for the final test.

The room was large, but there weren't many places to hide things. Since the account password was definitely stored at home, Grace's room was the most likely location.

Toys, clothes, picture books... She turned over every corner but found nothing.

###Chapter 842

From the live broadcast footage, she saw smiles on every face.

###Chapter 843

###Chapter 859

Wasn't this promotion speed a bit too exaggerated?

###Chapter 862

###Chapter 865

The sea shimmered with fragmented silver light.

A private yacht cut through the waves.

Evelyn Ross stood on the deck, the sea breeze lifting her long hair.

She gazed at the massive vessel and couldn't help but ask, "Yours?"

"Hmm."

Alexander Vance stood beside her, one hand in his pocket.

Evelyn clicked her tongue. "Extravagant."

A yacht capable of deep-sea voyages like this cost billions.

The Vance family was wealthy, but not to the point of casually buying toys of this caliber.

She turned her head to look at him. "What exactly do you do?"

Back in Aldoria, at Pirate Bay, he had managed things with ease.

Could it be...

Alexander chuckled softly. "Isn't it a bit late to ask now?"

He took a step closer, his breath brushing her ear. "Mrs. Vance, you boarded my ship long ago."

Evelyn's ears grew warm.

Alexander wrapped his arms around her waist from behind.

His voice was low in the wind. "Back when I was driven out of the Vance family, Grandma sent me abroad."

"During those years overseas, I didn't follow the conventional path of study."

"A few friends and I started a shipping company."

"Once, our cargo was hijacked by pirates."

Evelyn's heart skipped a beat.

She turned around, meeting his eyes.

Alexander continued, "I was young and reckless back then. I thought dying wouldn't matter much."

"So I hired a team of mercenaries and stormed the pirate island."

Evelyn's pupils contracted slightly. "You..."

"It was dangerous, I know." Alexander smiled. "But we won."

"Later, we realized seizing pirates' wealth was faster."

"So we took down island after island."

Evelyn stared at him, stunned.

This man was always like this.

Casually recounting heart-stopping past events.

She suddenly remembered his childhood.

Despised by his father, ostracized by his elder brother.

Only his grandmother protected him, but even she was powerless.

In the end, she could only send him away.

Evelyn knew the taste of lacking love herself.

But at least, she had Sophia Ashcroft.

What about Alexander?

Alone, struggling to survive in a foreign land.

"Don't ever do that again."

Her voice was muffled against his chest.

Alexander looked down. "Hmm?"

"You have me now." Evelyn looked up, her gaze serious. "I want you to live well."

A flicker of emotion passed through Alexander's eyes.

He raised his hand to stroke her cheek.

"Okay."

"Now, I don't need to take the field myself anymore."

"That stretch of sea is mostly pacified."

He paused, his voice softening further. "Besides, I can't let our future children live such a life on the edge."

Evelyn's face flushed.

"Who's having children with you..."

She pushed him away, turning to face the sea again.

But the tips of her ears were burning red.

Alexander chuckled softly, not teasing her further.

The yacht continued forward.

Finally, it stopped at a specific coordinate.

Any further would enter the Sterling Family's radar range.

Alexander took her hand.

"We need to switch to a smaller boat now."

He pointed below the railing.

A small speedboat bobbed with the waves.

Its hull was black, looking worn and shabby.

On the vast ocean, it resembled a leaf that could capsize at any moment.

Yet Evelyn didn't hesitate.

"You're risking your life with me. What do I have to fear?"

She clasped his hand in return.

Their fingers intertwined.

The two descended the gangway to the speedboat.

Only then did Evelyn realize this boat was not ordinary.

The exterior looked dilapidated, but the interior was equipped with sophisticated gear.

It had reinforced collision structures and an advanced navigation system.

Alexander explained, "A regular small boat would be gone with one wave."

"I modified it. It's safe enough."

Evelyn curved her lips into a smile.

"Then let's go."

Alexander started the engine.

The speedboat shot forward like an arrow, slicing through the water.

The yacht grew smaller behind them.

Eventually, it disappeared from sight.

Ahead lay endless darkness.

Waves slapped against the hull.

Evelyn sat beside Alexander.

Her hand never left his.

The small boat sailed steadfastly into the unknown.

Toward the place they had to go.

The sea wind howled.

The starlight dimmed.

But their direction never wavered.
###Chapter 866

The small boat rocked violently on the sea.

A wave crashed against it, tilting the hull sharply, almost capsizing it.

Alexander Vance steadied the helm, using some method to keep the boat stable.

Evelyn Ross sat on the deck beside him.

Moonlight spilled onto the sea, cold and intense.

"This sea," she said softly, "seems capable of swallowing everything."

It was too deep, too dark.

Pitch black.

Evelyn narrowed her eyes. "Our identities?"

"Eloping lovers." Alexander looked at her. "You caught the eye of a crime boss. I helped you escape. Now he's chasing us. We have to abandon ship, drift to the Sterling Family's island, become two homeless drifters."

Evelyn's lips twitched. "That's... too far-fetched, isn't it? A crime boss fancied me?"

"With your face, it's not strange." Alexander chuckled. "With my face, you'd be willing to elope with me, also not strange. Besides—"

He pointed to the distant cruise ship fading into the distance.

"The crime boss is on that ship."

In the half-month back in New York, she practiced swimming every day, just for this moment.

As soon as she spoke, Alexander pulled out a pistol, aimed at his own thigh, and pulled the trigger.

They were at sea. What if he was injured?!

Evelyn, eyes red, tore a strip from her own clothes, tightly wrapping his wound. "We could have made up another reason!"

"Evelyn Vance."

"I'm used to it." Alexander said. "Fought pirates before. A bullet nearly hit my heart. I survived."

Evelyn leaned against him silently.

"Okay."

Alexander pressed a button.

The boat noticeably lightened, rocking more violently in the waves.

Evelyn looked toward the Sterling Family island two kilometers away, a smile curling her lips.

She was back.

Just as the thought formed, a massive wave struck.

The boat capsized.
###Chapter 867

The wound on his leg was pale and waterlogged from the seawater.

The bleeding stopped temporarily.

But they needed to find a doctor urgently.

This was a beach.

There was no visible entrance.

Footsteps sounded.

A line of people in combat uniforms rushed towards them.

The leader stepped forward.

His voice was icy.

"Speak. Who are you?"
###Chapter 868

Evelyn wanted to stand up and speak.

###Chapter 869

Their enemies might be waiting outside, but they can't surround the entire island... Find a corner they won't notice and send them off quietly. The world outside is vast. They won't be able to find you."

"No buts!" Kingsley interrupted her, his tone firm. "You're worried, right? Fine. I'll personally escort them off the island. I'll guarantee their safe arrival on the mainland! Is that good enough?"

Having said that, he walked straight up to Evelyn and Alexander. His gaze was sharp as a knife, his tone carrying an undeniable warning. "You are outsiders. If you came here with ulterior motives, you won't leave. If not... then I've given my guarantee, and you should obey. I believe you know what choice to make, right?"

They had finally managed to get onto the island, and now they had to leave?
###Chapter 879

After all the trouble to set foot on this island, were they really going to be kicked out now?

Evelyn and Alexander were escorted in Kingsley's personal vehicle, with escort cars in front, behind, left, and right. The entourage was immense.

Dozens of black sedans protected their car in the middle, forming a moving wall of steel.

She looked at Alexander, her eyes asking: If we take him hostage, threaten these people to let us go, and then become drifters, is it feasible?

Alexander shook his head slightly, his gaze falling on Kingsley's left hand.

That hand was constantly resting on his waist—where a gun was holstered.

Evelyn's heart tightened.

The interior of the car was cramped. No matter how fast she moved, she couldn't outpace a bullet.

She could only resign herself with a sigh.

The motorcade passed through the bustling city center and finally stopped at the shore.

The vast blue sea stretched to the horizon. The sea breeze carried a salty, damp scent.

Evelyn looked at this sea, feeling only irony.

Had she come to save her mother only to turn this into a "Saint Helena Island day trip"?

Was she really going to be deported just like that?

Kingsley gave her no chance. He directly ordered the bodyguards to escort the two onto a speedboat.

The speedboat's engine roared, cutting through the sea surface as it sped toward the vast ocean.

She clenched her bound hands, her nails digging deep into her palms.

No.

She absolutely could not leave like this.

Her mother was still on this island.

She had to find a way back.

Evelyn looked at Alexander, her gaze resolute.

Alexander read the meaning in her eyes and gave a slight nod.

The bodyguard piloting the speedboat had his back to them, focused on the path ahead.

Now.

Alexander acted at the same time, seizing the steering wheel.

The speedboat rocked violently on the sea, carving a dangerous arc.

The icy seawater instantly swallowed her.

She struggled upward, breaking the surface just in time to see Alexander jump down as well.

The speedboat, out of control, crashed into a reef with a tremendous roar.

Evelyn and Alexander dove underwater, swimming in the opposite direction from the island.

They had to escape pursuit temporarily, then find a way to sneak back onto the island.

The seawater was bitingly cold. Evelyn gritted her teeth, paddling desperately.

Her mother was waiting for her.

She absolutely could not give up.

Night deepened. On the sea surface, only fragments of the speedboat wreckage remained, drifting with the waves.

Two figures had already vanished into the vast ocean.

When Kingsley received the news, his face turned ashen.

"They jumped?" He sneered coldly. "They have some skill. Pass the order: the entire island is on high alert. Strengthen patrols along the coastline. If they dare return, shoot on sight!"

He turned to look at the second-floor window of the villa, where Sienna's room light was still on.

This daughter was, after all, too naive.

He had to protect her, even if it meant using forceful methods.

Kingsley withdrew his gaze, his eyes profound.

This island was far from as peaceful as it appeared on the surface.

Evelyn and Alexander's intrusion might stir up even greater waves.

And he had to control everything.

On the sea, Evelyn and Alexander finally swam to a remote reef area.

The two climbed onto the rocks, soaked to the bone and utterly exhausted.

Evelyn gasped for breath, looking at the distant outline of the island.

The lights were brilliant, like a pearl on the sea.

"We'll go back," she said softly, her tone firm.

Alexander grasped her hand. "Yes."

The night was deep. The sea wind howled.

Their escape had only just begun.

And the secrets of this island were about to be uncovered.
###Chapter 880

The strength of the Sterling Family's main bloodline was indeed formidable.

At the horizon where the coastline ended, a small boat was cutting through the waves.

Several bodyguards stood with their hands clasped behind their backs, their gazes fixed on Evelyn Ross and Alexander Vance like hawks.

The two were escorted to the shore.
Once the boat was secured, they were roughly pushed aboard.

Evelyn quickly scanned the interior of the cabin.

The vessel wasn't large, but it was well-constructed with high safety standards.
The cabin was stocked with enough food and fresh water for six or seven days.
Life jackets, a compass, signal flares, and other survival tools were all present.
The boat's configuration was even more comprehensive than the one they had arrived in.

Evelyn and Alexander exchanged a glance.

Both sensed something was off.
Just moments ago, Kingsley Sterling had been accusing mainlanders of being cunning.
Yet now, he was sending them off in what could be described as a "luxury" escape vessel.
This change in attitude was too abrupt.
Would the Sterling Family be so considerate towards so-called "drifters"?

Unless... they weren't drifters at all.

A realization flashed in Evelyn's mind.
She looked sharply at Alexander.
He gave a slight nod, clearly having arrived at the same conclusion.

With a subtle twist of her wrist, the ropes binding her fell away.
She strode to the side of the boat and called out loudly, "Mr. Sterling, please wait."

Kingsley frowned and turned back, his tone cold.
"What is it now?"
Evelyn's gaze was firm.
"May we speak privately? After we talk, if you still wish to send us away, we will not utter another word of protest."

Kingsley was silent for a moment before finally waving his hand.
The bodyguards parted to create a path.

Evelyn jumped off the boat and walked up to Kingsley.
She lowered her voice and softly uttered two words.
"Uncle."

Kingsley's pupils contracted sharply.
He quickly suppressed the turmoil in his eyes and said coldly, "Nonsense."
Evelyn smiled.
"Uncle, you've already recognized me, haven't you?"
Kingsley took half a step back and snorted.
"Don't try to get familiar."

He turned to leave.

Evelyn's voice came from behind him, clear and forceful.
"Uncle, even if you send me away this time, I will definitely come back."

Kingsley's steps halted.
He slowly turned back to look at Evelyn.
That face, the spirit in her eyes and brows, overlapped with the memory of his sister.
How could he not recognize it?

It was just that the waters of the Sterling Family ran too deep.
After years of maneuvering, he still hadn't been able to rescue his sister.
What could Evelyn, coming alone, possibly do?
She would only put herself in danger.
That's why he wanted to send her away as quickly as possible.

But this niece... she was too much like her mother.
The same stubbornness.
The same sharpness.

I must save Mom."

"Your mother wouldn't want you to take this risk."

An unspoken understanding hung in the air.
It was the resoSterlingce of shared blood.

This uncle, meeting for the first time, must have also expended countless efforts over the years trying to rescue her mother, right?

Dozens of bodyguards surged from all directions, holding submachine guns, surrounding Kingsley, Evelyn, and their group.

"Don't move!"
The dark muzzles of the guns were all trained on them.

In the next second, Kingsley had already stepped in front of her.
Alexander also moved swiftly to her side, shielding her.

One in front, one beside.
Two men firmly protected her in the middle.

Scarlett Sterling, clinging to the arm of a middle-aged man, stepped out with an arrogant air.

###Chapter 881

Evelyn narrowed her eyes.

The atmosphere on the scene was taut as a bowstring.

Bodyguards on both sides held their breath, muscles tensed, eyes sharp, waiting for a single signal.

Scarlett lifted her chin, a smug curve on her lips. Her gaze swept dismissively over Evelyn and Alexander, her voice dripping with scorn. "Oppose me? You're not even worthy."

Sienna was of the main bloodline, her status exalted. Scarlett couldn't touch her.

Sebastian Sterling.

Two words, brooking no argument.

So.

Her premonition had not been wrong.

Sebastian's target had never been her and Alexander.

From the very beginning, what he wanted was Kingsley.

###Chapter 882

They had been rivals for half a lifetime. Kingsley had fallen from the main family line to a branch, while Sebastian had climbed from a branch to become the head of the family's trusted confidant. Their grudges were long past untangling.

But at their core, they were both men of the Sterling Family.

In this matriarchal clan, men were born as accessories, tools, shadows serving women. They had been overlooked together since childhood, sweating together on the training grounds, struggling together to prove their worth...

She knew this was her uncle sending her a message—Sienna would be safe if she didn't act recklessly; the women of the Sterling Family wouldn't be easily disposed of; and her mother, Sophia, was still alive.

"Dad! Let me go!"

"Let me go! Why are you stopping me? Evelyn, I've been so good to you! Why won't you let me save Dad!" Sienna's face was streaked with tears as she pounded on Evelyn's chest.

Evelyn said nothing.

Kingsley had been taken because of her mother.

Looking at Sienna, who had just lost her father, Evelyn's throat tightened.

She collapsed to the ground, tears falling drop by drop.

"After Aunt ran away, our family could never hold our heads high here... When I was little, Dad always said not to hate Aunt, that she had no choice. He protected us with everything he had, sheltered us under his wing... But now Dad's been taken too. What should I do? What do I do?"

Evelyn crouched down and wrapped her arms around Sienna's trembling shoulders. "Don't be afraid. I'm here. I will find a way to save Uncle."

She suddenly pointed at the yacht docked at the pier. "You should leave! I can't even protect myself now. I can't protect you. Leave this place. At least you won't be dragged into this."

Evelyn's eyes reddened.

After learning her identity, Kingsley's first instinct had been to send her away.

Sienna, timid as she was, had made the same first choice.

These were her family.

Her blood relatives.
###Chapter 883
